members.introduce: Former Vice-President for Institutional Advancement and Chair Professor at HKUST, currently President of the University of Hong Kong. PhD in Mathematics from Harvard University. Previously served at Georgia Institute of Technology and Michigan State University. Joined HKUST in 2014, served as Head of Department of Mathematics and Dean of School of Science.

members.name_desktop: Mr. Samuel Yung Wing Ki, SBS, MH, JP
members.introduce: Mr. Samuel Yung is an Executive District Director & Honorable Advisor of AIA International Limited. He is Vice Chairman of the Committee for Economic Affairs, Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) National Committee and Founding President of Hong Kong Professionals and Senior Executives Association. Mr. Yung has strong ties with the tertiary education sector. He is a Council Member of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) and a Court Member of the Hong Kong Metropolitan University (HKMU).

Prof. Kani Chen acts as program director of MSc in Financial Mathematics and CoDirector of Risk Management and Business Intelligence Program in HKUST. He received a PhD in Statistics (1994) from Columbia University in the City of New York, an MSc (1990) and a BSc (1987) from Peking University. He has over decades of research and teaching experience in financial mathematics.

Mr. Hyde Li, CFA, serves as the Executive Director of Tianlong Securities Co., Ltd. and the Chairman of Fund Connect HK Limited. He is also the President of the Hong Kong MBA Institute. Mr. Li has many years of experience in the traditional and digital asset investment industries. He has managed various prestigious projects, including the "Top 100 Listed Companies in Hong Kong" for Finet Group Limited, collaborated with Huobi Group on digital asset quantitative trading management, and handled asset management for family offices. He has built extensive professional networks and maintained strong connections with the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, providing a vast platform for student entrepreneurship and career development.

empowerFutureQuantLeaders: Empowering future quantitative finance leaders through knowledge transfer, networking, and competition practice
missionText: Bridging academia and industry, promoting practical applications in the field of quantitative finance through academic innovation, building a platform for international cooperation and exchange, and nurturing forward-looking and innovative quantitative professionals.
visionText: To become the engine shaping the future leaders of global quantitative trading, driving industry innovation and progress by establishing an open global knowledge-sharing network.
cultureText: Innovation-driven, resource-sharing, technology forefront – exploring future possibilities together.
researchDirectionsSubtitle: Exploring the frontiers of quantitative finance and building innovative research systems

researchTopics.title: Alpha New Paradigm: Multi-dimensional Signals & Intelligent Factor Mining
researchTopics.role: Vice President, Head of Factor & Model Research
researchTopics.description: Traditional factor research relies on manual enumeration, suffers from efficiency constraints and homogenization, and struggles to adapt to market regime changes. Pure deep learning models often fall into black boxes. We leverage LLM and reinforcement learning to drive automatic generation and iteration of interpretable factors, systematically mining multi-dimensional heterogeneous signals, extracting implicit embeddings through neural networks, and monitoring factor decay with Meta Alpha to continuously supplement effective Alpha adapted to new market environments.

researchTopics.title: Model & Compute Positioning in Low SNR Environments
researchTopics.role: Vice President, Head of Model Research
researchTopics.description: Blindly stacking parameters in monolithic universal models is merely a product of deterministic illusion, inevitably leading to sluggishness and overfitting when facing drastically switching markets. We abandon bloat and rigidity, instead building specialized model arrays dynamically dispatched by routing mechanisms according to market microstructure states, with real-time self-assessment and online fine-tuning. This relies not on parameter inflation, but on flexible compute allocation in uncertainty—adaptation always trumps rigidity.

researchTopics.title: Quantitative Development: Data & Research
researchTopics.role: Vice President, Head of QD&AI Technology
researchTopics.description: Python-centered QD research stacks emphasize vectorization and rapid experimentation, but easily produce PIT leakage, lineage breaks, and train-inference drift. We focus on bi-temporal data, feature contracts, and reproducible experiments, combining columnar computation, distributed DAG, and versioned data lakes to balance iteration efficiency, statistical validity, and auditability.

researchTopics.title: Portfolio Construction: Explicit Constraints & Global Optimization
researchTopics.role: Vice President, Head of Risk Control & Portfolio Optimization
researchTopics.description: Risk control and portfolio optimization always face a dilemma: traditional two-stage methods easily decouple signal prediction and portfolio decisions; end-to-end learning gets closer to investment objectives but faces overfitting and black-box risks. We focus on explicit predict-then-optimize architecture and differentiable convex optimization, combining multi-period control and distributionally robust methods, exploring risk-constrained offline reinforcement learning in scenarios like path dependence and non-convex trading constraints, balancing effectiveness, robustness, and auditability.

researchTopics.title: AI-driven Multi-modal Derivatives Research & Strategy Mining
researchTopics.role: Vice President, Head of Futures & Options Trading
researchTopics.description: Derivatives research faces challenges involving multi-source heterogeneous data and complex strategy search spaces. We integrate factors such as pricing, volume-price dynamics, and transmission mechanisms to build cross-asset, cross-frequency multi-modal signal systems, providing high-quality structured representations and prior information for models. Building on this foundation and combining cutting-edge large language model advances, we explore directions like code reinforcement and tree search, introducing strategy expression evolution and search methods to build an AI-assisted quantitative research framework.

researchTopics.title: Subjective-Quantitative Integration: Unified Modeling of Investment Views and Portfolio Policy
researchTopics.role: President, Head of Subjective-Quantitative Integration & Investment Decision
researchTopics.description: Subjective research and quantitative systems have long used different information expressions and decision languages, lacking a complete framework to uniformly map investment hypotheses, PM judgments, and risk preferences to "signal-model-investment policy." We combine Bayesian view fusion, decision-oriented learning, and human-machine collaboration methods to build a three-tier system: "ALPHA signal generation—PM return prediction and portfolio modeling—risk preference and strategy implementation," continuously calibrating views, models, and portfolio decisions through live attribution and dynamic feedback.

Through Knowledge Transfer, 
Networking, and Competitions
association_description_1: . As a student society of the HKUST Master of Science in Financial Mathematics (MAFM), we are committed to helping students enter the quantitative industry and build effective networks. Our alumni network covers over 10,000 HKUST graduates. Additionally, we plan to hold trading competitions for all students to discover talent and incubate future quant funds.
association_description_2: Since its establishment in 2006, the Department of Mathematics at HKUST enrolls about 800 undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students each year. As a student leadership platform supported by the department, our alumni network covers over 10,000 students and alumni.

timeline.eligibility_description: The competition is designed for current students and alumni of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and it also welcomes entries from students and alumni of other universities in Hong Kong and beyond.
timeline.registration_method_description: Submit team information on the official Quant Trading Society website.
timeline.qualification_review_stage: Qualification Review and Competition Registration Stage
timeline.sim_account_description: Fill out the registration form link to obtain an official competition simulation account.
timeline.team_strategy_review_description: Team members are reviewed based on certain rules; email contact may be required.
timeline.pre_competition_item_description: Assign simulation trading accounts; select team advisors; organize trading salons.
timeline.main_competition_item_description: Participants will trade using their official competition simulation accounts.
timeline.results_summary_description: Quant Trading Society will compile and verify all team data to form the final results.
timeline.strategy_defense_meeting_description: Representatives from the best performing teams will present at a defense meeting chaired by Quant Trading Society's honorary technical advisors.
timeline.judging_description: Judges will evaluate the trading strategies based on stability, profitability, risk management, and future performance expectations to determine the final rankings.
timeline.awards_ceremony_description: The competition results will be announced, and awards will be presented.

competition.title: Quant Trading Society Competition
competition.intro_part1: The Quant Trading Society will officially launch its second
competition.intro_part3: . The competition is designed for current students and alumni of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. It also welcomes entries from students and alumni of other universities in Hong Kong and beyond. Each team must be captained by a current student from a Hong Kong institution or an alum with Hong Kong residency.
competition.competition_details_part1: The simulation trading competition consists of a two-week preliminary round and a two-and-a-half-month final round, with only the results of the final round being considered for the final scores.
competition.competition_details_part2: Supported by Tiger Brokers, teams will have the flexibility to manage portfolios that may include stocks, commodities, ETFs, and derivatives, using various quantitative trading techniques to showcase their unique investment strategies.
